'''Robin Tonra Neumayer''' is an American mathematician, the recipient of the 2024 [[Sadosky Prize]] in [[mathematical analysis]]. Her research connects the [[calculus of variations]], [[partial differential equation]]s, and [[geometric analysis]],{{r|sadosky}} and includes the study of geometric aspects of [[Sobolev inequality|Sobolev-type inequalities]], [[isoperimetric inequality|isoperimetric inequalities]], and the [[Rayleigh–Faber–Krahn inequality]].{{r|career}} She is an assistant professor of mathematics at [[Carnegie Mellon University]].{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Neumayer majored in mathematics, with a business minor, at the [[University of South Carolina]]. She graduated [[summa cum laude]] in 2012. She continued her studies in mathematics at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], where she received a master's degree in 2014 and completed her Ph.D. in 2017.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Minimality and stability properties in Sobolev and isoperimetric inequalities'', was jointly supervised by [[Alessio Figalli]] and Francesco Maggi.{{r|cv|diss}} In her dissertation, she also cites Maria Girardi of the University of South Carolina as a mentor who strongly influenced her choice to continue in mathematics.{{r|diss}}

After postdoctoral study at [[Northwestern University]] in [[Chicago]] and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], she joined [[Carnegie Mellon University]] as a tenure-track Gregg Zeitlin Early Career Professor in 2021.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Neumayer is the 2024 recipient of the [[Sadosky Prize]] in analysis of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], given "for outstanding contributions to calculus of variations, partial differential equations, and geometric analysis".{{r|sadosky}} She also received a [[National Science Foundation CAREER Award]] in 2024.{{r|career}}
